source_note: RxNav's live Drug-Drug Interaction API was permanently discontinued by NLM in Jan 2024. This file is a manually curated rule set based on well-documented, publicly known interactions (ONC High-Priority style pairs), cross-referenced against openFDA label warnings. See README Scope & Limitations. Task 13 adds 28 rules that each cite FDA/DailyMed labels or regulator notices (see evidence_sources.json, SRC-CITED-*); all remain needs_clinical_review and are not clinically validated.

interaction_rules.description: Combined use significantly increases risk of bleeding due to additive anticoagulant/antiplatelet effects.
NSAIDs increase bleeding risk when combined with warfarin; also raises GI bleed risk independently.
Antibiotics can disrupt gut flora that synthesize vitamin K, potentiating warfarin's anticoagulant effect and raising INR.
Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, slowing clearance of the S-warfarin isomer and increasing INR and bleeding risk.
Thyroid hormone increases clotting factor turnover, potentiating warfarin's anticoagulant effect; INR should be monitored closely after any dose change.
Statins can mildly potentiate warfarin's anticoagulant effect via CYP interaction; periodic INR monitoring is generally advised.
Ibuprofen competitively blocks aspirin's irreversible binding to COX-1 on platelets, reducing aspirin's cardioprotective antiplatelet effect.
NSAIDs blunt the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and, combined, increase risk of reduced kidney function, especially with volume depletion.
NSAIDs can reduce the antihypertensive effectiveness of beta-blockers through sodium and fluid retention.
Reduced gastric acidity from PPIs impairs levothyroxine absorption; doses should be separated and thyroid function monitored.
ACE inhibitors can modestly increase insulin sensitivity, slightly raising hypoglycemia risk when combined with glucose-lowering agents.
Two antihypertensive agents used together have an additive blood-pressure-lowering effect; monitor for symptomatic hypotension, particularly at treatment initiation.
Amlodipine increases simvastatin exposure (CYP3A4), raising the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis; the simvastatin label limits the daily simvastatin dose (20 mg) when it is used with amlodipine.
interaction_rules.source: FDA ZOCOR label (2023); DailyMed simvastatin SPL; MHRA Drug Safety Update (Oct 2012)

interaction_rules.description: Amiodarone raises simvastatin plasma concentrations, increasing the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis; the labels cap the co-administered simvastatin dose (20 mg/day).
interaction_rules.source: FDA ZOCOR label (2023); DailyMed simvastatin and amiodarone SPLs

interaction_rules.description: Simvastatin can prolong the INR in patients taking coumarin anticoagulants; the simvastatin label advises INR monitoring when simvastatin is started, stopped, or its dose is changed.
Clarithromycin strongly inhibits CYP3A4 and markedly raises simvastatin exposure; concomitant use is contraindicated because of the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
interaction_rules.source: FDA BIAXIN label (2018), section 4; FDA ZOCOR label (2023)

interaction_rules.description: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and reduces formation of clopidogrel's active metabolite, diminishing its antiplatelet effect, including when doses are taken 12 hours apart; the clopidogrel label advises avoiding concomitant use of omeprazole or esomeprazole.
Concomitant NSAID use with clopidogrel increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
Clopidogrel did not change S-warfarin pharmacokinetics or INR in studies, but co-administration increases bleeding risk through independent effects on hemostasis.
SSRIs and SNRIs, including sertraline, impair platelet function and add to the bleeding risk of clopidogrel.
interaction_rules.source: FDA PLAVIX label (2019), section 7.5; FDA ZOLOFT label (2023), section 5.3

interaction_rules.description: Calcium carbonate can bind levothyroxine in the gut and reduce its absorption, risking hypothyroidism; the label advises administering levothyroxine at least 4 hours apart from calcium carbonate.

NSAIDs can elevate and prolong methotrexate levels, with reports of severe and sometimes fatal bone-marrow and gastrointestinal toxicity, mainly with high-dose methotrexate; caution and monitoring are advised at lower doses.
interaction_rules.source: FDA methotrexate label (2026), section 7.1; Can Fam Physician 2014, Table 1

interaction_rules.description: Salicylates, notably high-dose aspirin, can raise methotrexate exposure and the risk of bone-marrow suppression and other methotrexate toxicity.
interaction_rules.source: FDA methotrexate label (2026), section 7.1; Can Fam Physician 2014, Table 1

interaction_rules.description: Penicillins can reduce renal clearance of methotrexate, raising its levels and the risk of haematologic and gastrointestinal toxicity; close monitoring is advised.
interaction_rules.source: FDA methotrexate label (2026), section 7.1; Can Fam Physician 2014, Table 1

interaction_rules.description: Proton pump inhibitors may delay methotrexate elimination and raise its levels, mainly at high methotrexate doses; the evidence is largely case reports and population pharmacokinetic data.
interaction_rules.source: Pfizer Canada methotrexate monograph, section 9.4; FDA methotrexate label (2026), section 7.1

interaction_rules.description: Sildenafil potentiates the hypotensive effect of organic nitrates; co-administration, including nitroglycerin, is contraindicated because of the risk of severe, potentially life-threatening hypotension.
Sildenafil produces additional blood-pressure lowering when given with amlodipine; monitor for symptomatic hypotension.
Amiodarone potentiates warfarin's anticoagulant response and can result in serious or fatal bleeding; close INR monitoring is required.
Beta blockers add to amiodarone's negative chronotropic effects, which can cause bradycardia, sinus arrest, and AV block; heart rate should be monitored.
Amiodarone raises digoxin concentrations; the label advises reducing digoxin by half or discontinuing it, and monitoring for digoxin toxicity.
Amiodarone can raise plasma concentrations of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, including atorvastatin, increasing the risk of myopathy; a lower starting statin dose may be required.
Combining tramadol with serotonergic drugs such as sertraline increases the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures; use together only when clearly warranted and monitor for symptoms.
interaction_rules.source: FDA ULTRAM label (2023); FDA ZOLOFT label (2023), section 5.2

interaction_rules.description: Boxed warning: opioids used with benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants can cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death; concomitant use is reserved for patients without alternatives.
Postmarketing reports describe altered warfarin effect, including elevated INR, with tramadol; monitor INR and watch for bleeding.
SSRIs increase bleeding risk and can alter anticoagulant effect when combined with warfarin; the label advises careful INR monitoring when sertraline is started or stopped.
Aspirin and other antiplatelet drugs taken with sertraline increase the risk of bleeding, including gastrointestinal bleeding.
NSAIDs taken with sertraline increase the risk of bleeding, including gastrointestinal bleeding.
Clarithromycin can potentiate warfarin's anticoagulant effect, with reports of INR elevation and serious bleeding; INR should be monitored closely.
Clarithromycin raises atorvastatin exposure (CYP3A4 inhibition); rare rhabdomyolysis has been reported, and the lowest necessary statin dose and caution are advised.
Clarithromycin inhibits P-glycoprotein and can raise digoxin exposure, with reports of digoxin toxicity including potentially fatal arrhythmias; monitor digoxin concentrations.
